drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for bacterial infections of the respiratory tract, throat, sinuses, ear, lungs, or urinary tract.
precautions: Take with or immediately after food to prevent severe stomach cramps and nausea.
Complete the entire prescribed 5-7 day course even if symptoms disappear early.
Avoid alcohol during the course to prevent liver strain.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take at the start of a meal for optimal absorption and gastric comfort.

drugs.conditionHint: Used for respiratory chest infections, tonsillitis, sinusitis, ear infections, and skin infections.
precautions: Typically taken once daily for 3 or 5 days at the exact same hour.
Take either 1 hour before eating or 2 hours after a meal with plenty of water.
Inform your doctor if you experience rapid or irregular heartbeats.
drugs.foodInstructions: Best taken on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).

drugs.conditionHint: Used to treat uncomplicated typhoid fever, urinary tract infections, and bronchitis.
precautions: Take with food to minimize indigestion.
Do not skip doses; maintain 12-hour intervals.
Drink at least 2 liters of water daily while on this medication.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take after meals.

drugs.conditionHint: Relieves mild to moderate body pain, headache, dental ache, and reduces high fever.
precautions: Never exceed 4000mg (4 grams) within 24 hours to protect the liver.
Maintain a minimum 4 to 6-hour gap between doses.
Avoid concurrent alcohol consumption.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food. Taking with food prevents stomach acidity in sensitive individuals.

drugs.conditionHint: Reduces swelling, joint inflammation, dental pain, sprains, and fever.
precautions: Always take strictly AFTER a full meal or with milk to avoid gastritis or ulcers.
Avoid if you have active stomach ulcers, severe kidney disease, or bleeding disorders.
Often co-prescribed with an antacid (Pantoprazole) to protect the stomach lining.
drugs.foodInstructions: Always take with food or milk.

drugs.conditionHint: Strong painkiller for muscular aches, toothaches, joint pain, and inflammatory fevers.
precautions: Must be taken after meals. Do not take on an empty stomach.
Do not take additional Paracetamol while using Combiflam.
Use shortest duration necessary (3-5 days).
drugs.foodInstructions: Take after meals.

drugs.conditionHint: Treats acid reflux, heartburn, GERD, and protects the stomach lining against NSAID painkillers.
precautions: Take on an empty stomach, ideally 30-45 minutes before breakfast.
Swallow whole; do not crush or chew the enteric-coated tablet.
Long-term continuous use (>1 year) should be monitored for B12/magnesium levels.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take 30 minutes before the first meal of the day.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for acid reflux accompanied by nausea, vomiting, fullness, or dyspepsia.
precautions: Take once daily on an empty stomach 30 minutes before breakfast.
Do not exceed recommended duration without physician review.
Notify physician if you have a history of cardiac arrhythmias.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take strictly 30 minutes before morning breakfast.

drugs.conditionHint: Lowers high blood pressure (hypertension) and prevents chest pain (angina).
precautions: Take at the exact same time every day for consistent 24-hour pressure control.
Do not discontinue abruptly, as blood pressure may spike rebound.
May cause mild ankle swelling or dizziness when standing up.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food, preferably morning.

drugs.conditionHint: Protects against heart attacks, strokes, and treats chronic high blood pressure.
precautions: Do not take during pregnancy; report pregnancy immediately to doctor.
Avoid potassium supplements or potassium-rich salt substitutes without medical testing.
Check blood pressure periodically and record values.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with or without food at the same hour each day.

drugs.conditionHint: First-line medicine to control high blood sugar in patients with Type 2 Diabetes.
precautions: Take with or immediately after meals to reduce gastrointestinal discomfort or loose stools.
Stay well-hydrated. Avoid heavy alcohol intake.
Temporarily withhold before medical imaging tests requiring iodinated contrast dye.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with or immediately after food.

drugs.conditionHint: Lowers 'bad' LDL cholesterol and triglycerides, reducing the risk of heart attacks and stroke.
precautions: Best taken at bedtime, as cholesterol synthesis peaks during the night.
Avoid drinking large quantities of grapefruit juice (interferes with statin breakdown).
Report unexplained muscle soreness, weakness, or tenderness promptly.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take at night before sleep, with or without food.

drugs.conditionHint: Relieves allergic rhinitis, runny nose, sneezing, pollen allergy, and allergic asthma flare-ups.
precautions: Take once daily in the evening, as levocetirizine can cause mild drowsiness.
Avoid driving or alcohol until you know how this medication affects your alertness.
Do not discontinue abruptly during allergy season without medical advice.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take at night before bedtime, with or without water.

drugs.conditionHint: Treats allergic skin rashes, hives, seasonal hay fever, and itchiness without making you drowsy.
precautions: Take with plain water. Avoid taking with fruit juices (apple, orange, grapefruit) within 4 hours.
Do not take antacids containing aluminum or magnesium within 2 hours of this tablet.
Safe for daytime work and driving.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with water on an empty stomach or with a light meal. Avoid citrus fruit juices.

drugs.salt: Calcium Carbonate (1250mg eq to 500mg elemental Ca) + Vitamin D3 (250 IU)
drugs.conditionHint: Strengthens bones and teeth, prevents osteoporosis, and meets calcium needs.
precautions: Take after meals; calcium carbonate requires stomach acid for maximum absorption.
Separate by at least 2 hours from thyroid medicine (Thyronorm) or iron supplements.
Drink plenty of water throughout the day.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with or right after lunch or dinner.

drugs.conditionHint: Promotes recovery from infection, relieves mouth ulcers, and boosts metabolic immunity.
precautions: May cause bright yellow urine — this is completely harmless riboflavin (Vit B2) excretion.
Take in the morning or afternoon with food to prevent mild nausea.
Keep the capsule strip away from moisture and heat.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take after breakfast.

drugs.conditionHint: Prevents blood clot formation, reducing the risk of heart attacks and strokes.
precautions: Swallow whole after food. Do not chew enteric-coated tablet.
Do NOT combine with painkillers like Brufen/Diclofenac without explicit doctor approval.
Inform dentists or surgeons that you are on blood-thinning aspirin before any procedure.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take after meals.

drugs.conditionHint: Broad-spectrum antibiotic prescribed for bacterial infections of the throat, chest, sinuses, ear, urinary tract, and skin. The clavulanic acid component protects the amoxicillin from bacterial resistance.
precautions: Take with or immediately after food to prevent nausea and stomach cramps.
Complete the entire prescribed course (typically 5–7 days) even if you feel better early.
Inform your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin before taking this drug.
Avoid alcohol during the course as it may increase side-effect severity.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take at the start of a meal for best absorption and minimal gastric irritation.

drugs.class: NSAID Analgesic + Antipyretic + Proteolytic Enzyme (Triple Action)
drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for acute pain with inflammation, post-surgical edema, dental pain, musculoskeletal pain, and fever. Serratiopeptidase reduces post-injury tissue swelling faster than NSAIDs alone.
precautions: Take strictly after food — Diclofenac on an empty stomach can cause gastric ulcers.
Do not take with other NSAIDs (Aspirin, Ibuprofen) simultaneously — risk of GI bleed.
Use for short-term acute pain only; do not exceed the prescribed duration.
Avoid in patients with kidney disease or history of stomach ulcers.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take immediately after a meal to protect stomach lining.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for rapid relief of bronchospasm in asthma and COPD, as well as nasal congestion. Levosalbutamol has fewer cardiac side effects than standard Salbutamol (Albuterol).
precautions: Shake well before every use. Use correct inhalation/spray technique for full dose delivery.
Do not exceed the prescribed number of puffs/actuations per dose to avoid tremors or palpitations.
Carry this as a rescue inhaler — do not use as a substitute for long-term controller medicine.
Inform your doctor if you need it more than 3 times per week; this may signal worsening asthma control.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be used anytime, independent of meals. Rinse mouth with water after inhalation use.

drugs.conditionHint: Commonly prescribed for fever, mild-to-moderate pain, headache, and body ache associated with viral infections.
precautions: Do not exceed 4g (4000mg) of paracetamol in 24 hours from all sources.
Avoid alcohol — combining with alcohol greatly raises risk of liver toxicity.
Check all other medications you are taking for hidden paracetamol content.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food.

drugs.class: Leukotriene Receptor Antagonist + Antihistamine (Allergy & Asthma Combo)
drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for allergic rhinitis, urticaria (hives), and seasonal allergies. The combination controls both inflammatory (leukotriene) and histamine pathways for dual-action allergy relief.
precautions: Take at night — Levocetirizine causes significant drowsiness and impairs driving.
Do not operate heavy machinery after taking this medicine.
Avoid alcohol as it potentiates CNS sedation.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food. Best at bedtime.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for common cold, flu, and upper respiratory tract infections. Provides combined antipyretic (paracetamol), antihistamine (cetirizine), nasal decongestant (phenylephrine), and alertness-restoring (caffeine) effects.
precautions: Avoid taking with other paracetamol-containing medicines to prevent overdose.
Phenylephrine component can raise blood pressure — use with caution in hypertensive patients.
Do not drive if feeling sedated from Cetirizine.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take after food to reduce nausea.

drugs.conditionHint: First-line treatment for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. Lowers blood glucose by reducing hepatic glucose production and improving peripheral insulin sensitivity.
precautions: Take with meals to minimize GI side effects (nausea, diarrhea).
Do NOT take if you have kidney disease (eGFR < 30) as it can cause lactic acidosis.
Inform your doctor before any contrast imaging (CT/MRI) — metformin must be withheld.
Alcohol magnifies the risk of hypoglycemia — avoid excessive intake.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with or immediately after a meal. Never on an empty stomach.

drugs.conditionHint: Combination prescribed for hypertension (high blood pressure). Telmisartan blocks angiotensin II receptors to relax blood vessels; Hydrochlorothiazide removes excess sodium and water via urine.
precautions: Take at the same time each day. Do not skip doses — sudden blood pressure spikes can cause strokes.
Monitor potassium levels — thiazide diuretics can cause hypokalemia.
Limit high-potassium foods if combined with potassium supplements.
Avoid dehydration in hot weather while on diuretics.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take at the same time each day, with or without food. Morning dosing preferred.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for Vitamin D deficiency or insufficiency. Essential for calcium absorption, bone mineralization, immune function, and mood regulation.
precautions: Take once weekly (or as prescribed). High-dose Vitamin D is taken in loading doses — do not increase frequency.
Dissolve sachet in water or milk and consume immediately.
Regular monitoring of serum Vitamin D levels is recommended during supplementation.
Avoid Vitamin D toxicity — do not self-supplement beyond prescribed dose.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take with a fat-containing meal (milk, ghee, nuts) for best absorption — Vitamin D is fat-soluble.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for moderate pain, dental pain, menstrual pain, muscle aches, and fever. The dual-action combination provides faster and stronger pain relief than either drug alone.
precautions: Take strictly after food — Ibuprofen on an empty stomach causes gastric erosion.
Do not combine with other NSAIDs or blood thinners.
Avoid in patients with peptic ulcers, kidney disease, or heart failure.
Short-term use only; do not exceed 5 days without medical advice.
drugs.foodInstructions: Always take immediately after a full meal.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for urinary tract infections, typhoid fever, respiratory infections, gonorrhea, and tonsillitis. A broad-spectrum antibiotic effective against resistant bacterial strains.
precautions: Complete the full antibiotic course to prevent antibiotic resistance.
Inform your doctor of any cephalosporin or penicillin allergy — cross-reactivity possible.
May cause diarrhea — stay hydrated and inform doctor if it becomes severe.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food. With food reduces GI upset.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for hypertension, heart failure, and kidney protection in diabetic patients. Widely used first-line blood pressure medication globally.
precautions: Dry cough is a very common side effect — inform your doctor if persistent.
Do NOT take during pregnancy — causes fetal harm (Category D/X).
Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless directed.
Do not stop abruptly — taper under medical supervision.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food at the same time each day.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed to reduce LDL (bad cholesterol) and triglycerides, and to lower risk of cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke) in high-risk patients.
precautions: Take at night — cholesterol is synthesized more actively during sleep, making evening dosing more effective.
Avoid grapefruit juice — it significantly increases statin blood levels, raising toxicity risk.
Report unexplained muscle pain, weakness, or dark urine immediately (possible rhabdomyolysis).
This is a long-term medication — do not stop without medical advice even if you feel fine.
drugs.foodInstructions: Preferably take in the evening or at night, with or without food.

drugs.conditionHint: Broad-spectrum antibiotic for ear infections (otitis media), strep throat, tonsillitis, bronchitis, and urinary tract infections.
precautions: Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms resolve early.
Inform doctor of any penicillin allergy — anaphylaxis risk.
Can cause mild rash in patients with infectious mononucleosis — inform your doctor.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for urinary tract infections, chest infections, bone/joint infections, gastroenteritis, and typhoid. One of the most widely prescribed antibiotics globally.
precautions: Take on an empty stomach or 2 hours after a meal for best absorption.
Avoid antacids, iron, and calcium supplements within 2 hours of dosing — they reduce absorption.
Stay well-hydrated — drink plenty of water to prevent kidney crystal formation.
Avoid prolonged sun exposure — ciprofloxacin causes photosensitivity.
drugs.foodInstructions: Ideally take on an empty stomach. Drink 2 full glasses of water with each dose.

drugs.class: Proton Pump Inhibitor (PPI) — Gastric Acid Suppressant
drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for GERD (acid reflux), gastric ulcers, erosive esophagitis, and stomach protection during NSAID therapy. A stronger and longer-lasting acid blocker than Omeprazole.
precautions: Take 30–60 minutes before the first meal of the day for maximum effectiveness.
Do not crush or chew — swallow whole to preserve enteric coating.
Long-term use (>1 year) can reduce magnesium and calcium absorption — monitor with doctor.
Can mask symptoms of gastric cancer — inform your doctor of persistent heartburn.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take 30–60 minutes before breakfast on an empty stomach.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed to reduce high LDL ('bad') cholesterol and triglycerides in blood, raise HDL ('good') cholesterol, and prevent heart attacks and strokes.
precautions: Take once daily preferably in the evening or at bedtime with water.
Strictly avoid grapefruit juice as it increases drug accumulation and muscle toxicity risk.
Promptly report any unexplained muscle aches, tenderness, or weakness to your doctor.
Periodic liver function tests (LFT) and lipid profile checks are recommended.
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food, preferably after dinner or at bedtime with a glass of water.

drugs.conditionHint: Prescribed for acute severe pain, swelling, tooth extraction, post-operative inflammation, and musculoskeletal injury.
precautions: Always take with or immediately after food to shield the stomach lining.
Do not combine with other painkillers or cold syrups containing paracetamol.
Avoid alcohol during treatment to prevent severe gastric mucosal irritation.
drugs.foodInstructions: Always take after a solid meal with water. Never take on an empty stomach.

drugs.conditionHint: Effective relief for joint pain, arthritis, backache, spondylitis, and headache.
precautions: Take after meals to avoid gastrointestinal discomfort.
Not recommended for patients with active peptic ulcers without PPI protection.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take strictly after meals with water.

drugs.salt: Vitamin B-Complex (B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B12)
drugs.conditionHint: Treats vitamin B deficiencies, peripheral neuropathy, nerve tingling/numbness, and fatigue.
precautions: Safe for long-term daily supplementation.
May cause harmless bright yellow coloration of urine due to Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin).
drugs.foodInstructions: Take in the morning with or after breakfast with water.

alternatives.brand: PMBJP Jan Aushadhi Vitamin B-Complex with B12

drugs.conditionHint: Corrects severe Vitamin D deficiency, supports immune health, bone mineralization, and neuromuscular function.
precautions: Take strictly ONCE A WEEK as prescribed by doctor. Do NOT take daily.
Best absorbed with a meal containing dietary fats (milk, ghee, or nuts).
drugs.foodInstructions: Take once weekly with warm milk or after a meal containing fat.

drugs.conditionHint: Reduces the risk of ischemic stroke and heart attack in patients with recent heart attacks or stents.
precautions: Take consistently at the same time every day.
Avoid combining with omeprazole without cardiologist guidance (use pantoprazole instead).
drugs.foodInstructions: Can be taken with or without food at the same time each day.

drugs.conditionHint: Treats high blood pressure (hypertension) with kidney protection and lower incidence of pedal ankle swelling.
precautions: Take consistently every morning.
Avoid abrupt discontinuation to prevent rebound hypertension.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take in the morning after breakfast.

drugs.conditionHint: Replaces missing thyroid hormone in hypothyroidism, sluggish metabolism, and post-thyroidectomy.
precautions: Strictly take FIRST THING IN THE MORNING with plain water on an empty stomach.
Wait at least 45 to 60 minutes before having tea, coffee, breakfast, or calcium supplements.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take 45–60 mins before morning tea/breakfast on an empty stomach with plain water.

drugs.conditionHint: Relieves menstrual period pain, abdominal colic spasms, intestinal cramps, and kidney stone colic.
precautions: Take only as needed for acute pain/cramps.
Always take after food to prevent stomach irritation.
drugs.foodInstructions: Take strictly after meals with plenty of water.
